question.leadin: Identify these politicians who were powerful during the 1990's.
question.text: This Georgia Republican served as Speaker of the House from 1995 to 1999 and was a co-writer of the Contract with America.
question.clue: This former Speaker of the House from Georgia won the South Carolina primary. During the campaign, he proposed a moon colony that could petition to become a U.S. state.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Republican Presidential hopefuls in the 2012 primary season.
swap.text: After only being allowed to compete in a small number of debates, this former New Mexico governor ran for president with the backing of the Libertarian Party.
swap.clue: This politician was referred to as "Puff Daddy" by Clinton drug czar Barry McCaffrey for his endorsement of marijuana legalization.

question.text: The Saturday Night Massacre was completed when Nixon made this third man the acting Attorney General and got him to fire Cox. In 1987, President Reagan nominated this man to the Supreme Court, but the Senate voted him down.
question.clue: As Solicitor General, this man ultimately carried out Nixon's order to fire special prosecutor Archibald Cox.

swap.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
swap.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

question.leadin: Answer the following about another drink-related political organization, the Tea Party.
question.text: The Tea Party first made a big splash in the midterm elections when they endorsed this Republican candidate who ousted Martha Coakley in the Massachusetts special election.
question.clue: This politician from Massachusetts who was beaten by Elizabeth Warren in his 2012 re-election bid.

swap.text: Name this governor whose failed 2012 presidential bid was partly blamed on the fact that he wanted to cut the Departments of Commerce, Education, and, um....oops.

question.leadin: This election's eventual winner emerged victorious following the Supreme Court's overturning of a prior ruling requiring a recount in Florida.
question.text: Name this election decided following the Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore.
question.clue: In another state during this election, N. Sanders Sauls became involved in the contest phase of the election after Katherine Harris ended the protest phase.

swap.text: This Democratic Party stalwart and Mayor of Chicago from 1955 to 1976 was an alleged racist and was accused of corruption several times.

question.text: Odierno assumed command of Iraq's Multi-National Force after this Four Star General, who holds a doctorate from Princeton, became head of U.S. Central Command in October 2008. He was the subject of a controversial 2007 ad placed in the New York Times by MoveOn.org.
question.clue: A 2007 advertisement from MoveOn.org claimed this man was "cooking the books for the White House."

question.text: No candidate won a majority in the 1992 election largely because this Texas billionaire received nineteen percent of the popular vote.
question.clue: This Texas businessman who received 18.9% of the popular vote but no electoral votes in a certain election.

swap.leadin: The evil of this figure radiates clearly from his bald pate and savagely grinning countenance, which resemble those of fictional evildoers Lex Luthor and Voldemort.
swap.text: Who is this governor-elect of Florida, to that state's eternal shame?
swap.clue: In 2010, Jeromy helped elect this tea-party aligned conservative as governor of Florida. This bald businessman narrowly defeated Democrat Alex Sink in the general election.

question.leadin: Name the following about works of importance in American race relations.
question.text: This famous essay collection by Cornell West includes sections on Black nihilism, Black leadership, and the relations between black people and Jewish people.

swap.text: This old friend of Hillary Clinton would serve as a White House counsel in early 1993. He was found dead that year, but despite conspiracy theories, every investigation has determined his death to be a suicide.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Republican Revolution of 1994.
question.text: This Georgia representative replaced Bob Michel as leader of the Republicans in the House, ascending to the office of Speaker in 1994. About a year later, his standoff with Clinton led to a government shutdown.

swap.leadin: The Conestoga Wood Specialties company joined this company in its 2014 lawsuit against the Affordable Care Act's contraceptive mandate.
swap.text: Name this company which, in June 2014, won a namesake case allowing it to deny employees birth control coverage.
swap.clue: This craft store chain that won a 2014 Supreme Court case against the federal government over their opposition to birth control requirements in the Affordable Care Act.

question.leadin: Answer the following about theories of counterinsurgency and guerilla warfare.
question.text: This general was chiefly responsible for the U.S. Army Counterinsurgency Field Manual, which he brought into practice as commander of the "Surge" during the Iraq War.
question.clue: That king of this name expelled the Seljuk Turks from his nation at the Battle of Didgori ], later moving his center to Tbilisi.

question.leadin: The winning candidate in this election made such bloopers as saying that Pearl Harbor occurred on September 7 and that he stood for "anti-Semitism." Answer the following about the election of 1988.
question.text: Possibly the most exciting moment in the campaign occurred in the vice-presidential debates when this Dukakis running mate and Texas Senator sneered that Dan Quayle was "no Jack Kennedy."
question.clue: He became president of Lincoln Consolidated during a fifteen-year absence from politics, which ended when he defeated George Bush in a 1970 election for senator from Texas.
